reproduce.docker: docker build -f automation/disk_heap_bench.Dockerfile -t diskheap-bench <context> && python3 automation/disk_heap_benchmark.py --include-network --docker --tasks hi,code --vmmalloc-so <path-to>/libvmmalloc.so.1 ...

verdicts.memtier: incompatible with the Bun-compiled OpenCode binary: transparent LD_PRELOAD works on trivial binaries and moves malloc traffic to FS_DAX file tiers, but the real agent segfaults deterministically (3/3 hi-task runs, exit -11 after a ~32 s stall; code-task runs OOM first). Not useful, not wired into production.
verdicts.overall: No candidate converts the 512 MB no-swap workload from unreliable/OOM to repeatable success. ~440 MB of the ~600 MB peak sits in [anon:WKFastMalloc], [anon:JSGigacage], [anon:JSJITCode], [anon:JSStructureHeap] and plain anonymous mmap segments that bypass libc malloc by design, so no LD_PRELOAD malloc interposer can move them. No production wrapper is implemented; Render Free remains unsuitable for real agent runs per issue #9 criteria.
verdicts.shim: partially works: the minimal custom MAP_SHARED shim is correct (stress-tested) and transparent, but moves only ~0.1-0.8 MB of ~600 MB, proving ~0% of the footprint travels through libc malloc-family paths after startup. Benchmark probe only; never ship it.
verdicts.smol: minor help only: BUN_OPTIONS=--smol cuts ~40 MB (~7%) off peak, still OOMs at 512 MB without swap. Keep as a harmless default, not a fix.
verdicts.userfaultfd: unsuitable: unprivileged userfaultfd returns EPERM on this kernel config and no maintained transparent wrapper exists for an unmodified Bun/JSC binary. No pager was built.
verdicts.vmmalloc: partially works: loads on ordinary disk with glibc 2.39, interposes malloc and serves it from a MAP_SHARED pool file, but moves only ~1-3 MB of ~600 MB (0.2-0.5%). Peak unchanged; 512 MB no-swap runs still OOM. Not useful, not wired into production.
